- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days), then underestimates later.
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in history (e.g., 82.31 → 85.72), then fails to correct downward.
- Underestimates when true price drops sharply (e.g., 83.26 → 78.20), often by 5–10%.
- Shows mean reversion bias: forecasts tend to revert to recent history but too slowly, missing sudden reversals.
- Lags in response to recent price drops: model takes 2–3 days to adjust downward after a true drop.
- Overconfident in short-term momentum: forecasts often assume continuation of recent trend, ignoring volatility or policy shocks.
- Underestimates volatility in late forecast horizon (last 5–10 days), especially when true price shows erratic or downward movement.
- Tends to overfit to recent high prices (last 5–7 days), ignoring longer-term mean or seasonal patterns.
- Fails to account for policy-driven price corrections (e.g., auction adjustments, cap changes) in the 10–15 day window.
